assessments.reasoning: The three verified publisher slices provide the alternative status tests, the mandatory distribution clause and the notice it identifies. Together they distinguish the basis of incompatibility from the resulting notice obligation.

challenge.method: Compared an exhibit printed in the license document, a notice attached to the Covered Software by the initial Contributor, and prior availability under MPL 1.1 or earlier without a Secondary License. Then varied the history to include a Secondary License.
challenge.results: The accompanying document alone does not establish the act specified in section 1.5(a). Actual attachment independently establishes ground (a). The specified prior history independently establishes ground (b) and triggers section 10.4 on the stated distribution. Prior availability also under a Secondary License defeats ground (b) but leaves ground (a) to be examined.

limitations: Actual attachment, the identity of the initial Contributor, licensing history and the chosen form and terms of distribution require evidence for any particular source.
reasoning: Section 10.4 requires attachment of the Exhibit B notice upon distribution under MPL 2.0 of source that meets either ground of incompatibility in section 1.5. Incompatibility can therefore trigger an attachment duty even when there was no previous attachment.
